sources_considered.why: Primary contemporary experiments on multiplication and transfer beyond training complexity.
Material counterevidence showing improved arithmetic transfer, with explicit limits on what priming achieves.
Reviewed the paper discussed in the post. Its digit-range analysis mixes operations and adds longer examples to training; the selected multiplication study more directly tests the criterion.

evidence_items.explanation: The study reports poor transfer beyond training complexity after GPT3 fine-tuning, including multiplication. It also reports only 55% and 59% accuracy for ChatGPT and GPT4 on three-digit multiplication, supporting the observed reliability limitation.

Specialized transformers reached 95% accuracy on 35-by-3-digit multiplication after training-set priming, demonstrating meaningful progress. However, priming supplied examples at target lengths, and the study found no transfer to omitted lengths; this does not satisfy the unseen-length contradiction condition.

unresolved_gaps: The studies cannot establish that every contemporary LLM lacked an internal multiplication algorithm.
No agreed numerical threshold defines reliable abstraction.
Exact experiment dates are not reported; event dates use the studies' reporting year.
